newsitem.title: USA: TWA ends lengthy search for chairman, CEO.
newsitem.headline: TWA ends lengthy search for chairman, CEO.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc late Wednesday elected Gerald Gitner its new chairman and chief executive officer, ending a search that began last fall, the company said.
A TWA spokesman told Reuters that Gitner, who was named vice chairman and acting chief executive officer in December, had turned down the board's repeated requests to accept the posts.

"Jeffrey Erickson (the company's former president and chief executive officer) announced last fall he would be leaving in mid-January," TWA spokesman John McDonald said. "He officially left TWA on December 16."

Gitner had been one of three interim executives at the nation's seventh-largest carrier. The company said Wednesday that David Kennedy would remain interim chief operating officer and Bill Compton would continue as acting vice-president-operations. Thomas Meagher will remain chairman of the board's executive committee, TWA said.

Industry analysts speculated in late December that TWA would remain an unlikely acquisition target as long as its top management was in flux, adding that the chief executive position was a difficult post to fill.
Meanwhile, Gitner will have several issues to address as TWA's chief executive officer.

Earlier this month, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers unanimously voted "no confidence" in Gitner as acting chief executive and called for him to step down in 60 days or less.
At the time, Gitner said he was "dismayed" by the union's position and did not address the call for his resignation.
Union officials were unavailable for comment on Gitner's appointment late Wednesday.
TWA also has five labor contracts coming up for renewal this fall, making it a likely target for labor unrest, analysts said.
Additionally, the carrier's fleet is the oldest among major U.S. carriers, with an average age of about 18.6 years.
The industry average age is about 11.9 years.
Last month, TWA also denied reports in USA Today that it met with investor Brian Freeman, which reportedly proposed a deal to take control of the carrier.
